note: Label audit of the replacement emails by Claude subagents on 2026-11-24: two reads each, mixed with untouched emails, blind to detector scores and to which emails were replacements. Round 1 covered the 9 first replacements; round 2 the two that were rewritten again. An LLM review, not a human hand-check.

reviews.reason: Sender claims to be Finance Operations at Merefield Health Group but writes from a personal mailbox on an odd lookalike domain and pushes a replacement invoice attachment with a soft deadline. Weak: the domain mismatch is the only pointable element and the tone is otherwise that of a normal colleague.
reviews.evidence: m.ellison@merefield-health-documents.example; "I've attached the updated copy as Invoice_Westbridge_Nov24.pdf ... this should replace the version I sent over last week"

reviews.reason: Reads as an ordinary friendly colleague email with an updated invoice attached; there is no pressure beyond a mild Friday deadline, no payment or credential request. The only cue is the sender domain merefield-health-documents.example versus the signed organisation Merefield Health Group, which a reader cannot confirm is a lookalike from the text alone.
reviews.evidence: m.ellison@merefield-health-documents.example; "I've attached the updated copy as Invoice_Westbridge_Nov24.pdf ... Could you have a look when you get a chance"

reviews.reason: Claims to be Alderwick Bank but the sender domain is unrelated to a bank domain and it pushes a named statement attachment. Subtle: no urgency and it says no action is required, so the domain is the only giveaway.
reviews.evidence: notices@alderwick-document-review.example; "Please open the attached document, Alderwick_Statement_November.pdf"

reviews.reason: Calm statement-ready notice that explicitly says no action is required, with no threat, link, credential or payment request. The only cue is the sender domain alderwick-document-review.example, which does not match a bank-style domain for Alderwick Bank, plus the statement being sent as an attachment; a reader could go either way.
reviews.evidence: notices@alderwick-document-review.example; "Please open the attached document, Alderwick_Statement_November.pdf ... No action is required if the statement is accurate."

reviews.reason: Claims to be Bellmont Bank but is sent from a hyphenated lookalike domain and pushes an unsolicited named attachment with an acknowledgment deadline. Subtle: the domain is the only giveaway, the body text is otherwise benign.

reviews.reason: Polite, personalised, routine annual-review letter with no threat, no credential or payment request and a relaxed deadline; nothing in the body is fraudulent. The only cue is the sender domain bellmont-bank-documents.example versus the claimed Bellmont Bank, which could equally be read as a bank's document-services domain.
reviews.evidence: client.records@bellmont-bank-documents.example; "Please find the attached file, Whitmore_Annual_Account_Review.pdf, and review the information at your earliest convenience."
